subject.title: Control-plane hardening from Optimus ops findings

question: Should `openclaw diagnose --json` become a stable versioned operator API that writes baseline, probe-cache, and incident records while collecting diagnostics?
rationale: The command’s public schema and write-on-diagnose semantics create durable product, automation, storage, and compatibility commitments that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Approve after redesign
options.body: Keep the diagnose API, but require SQLite-backed state, a narrow stable schema, and explicit exact-head redaction and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep diagnose read-only
options.body: Emit the diagnostic snapshot without persistent writes and move baseline, cache, and incident capture into separately named operator commands or services.

options.title: Pause the unified API
options.body: Land only independently useful internal hardening pieces and defer the public diagnose contract until its ownership and persistence model are designed.

recommendation.title: Approve after redesign
recommendation.body: Keep the diagnose API, but require SQLite-backed state, a narrow stable schema, and explicit exact-head redaction and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available adjacent routing candidate for status visibility and operator-facing control-plane behavior, although direct ownership evidence is limited.
